Maya: Heads-up: noticed a spike where account health scores jumped to green after CRM dedupe job last week. Suspect merged contacts duplicated "engagement" metrics into account-level aggregates.
Rafael: Do you have an example account id?
Maya: AC-7789. Before merge: 3 contacts, 1 active; post-merge: 6 contacts, 5 active, computed weekly_logins doubled.
Priya: That would inflate the engagement_weight in the healthscore. We should pause any automatic renewal nudges for affected accounts until we validate.
Sam: Agree. Quick mitigation: add a playbook predicate `dedupe_flag=true` to route those accounts to a low-urgency queue.
Maya: Proposed steps: (1) identify accounts with recent contact merges (dedupe_reason != null and dedupe_ts >= now() - interval '14 days'), (2) recompute healthscore using unique_user_count instead of raw contact_event_count for a canary slice, (3) set `dedupe_flag=true` and `dedupe_review_required=true` on those accounts.
Priya: SQL to find candidates: ```
SELECT a.account_id, a.health_score, count(distinct c.contact_id) as unique_contacts, sum(c.login_count) as contact_logins, a.last_dedupe_ts
FROM crm.accounts a
JOIN crm.contacts c ON c.account_id = a.account_id
WHERE a.last_dedupe_ts >= now() - interval '14 days'
GROUP BY a.account_id, a.health_score
ORDER BY a.last_dedupe_ts DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Rafael: For recompute logic, we can run a backfill that calculates engagement_metric = sum(distinct contact.user_id login_events) across sessions for the last 30 days. If engagement_metric decreases by >30% vs current value, mark for manual review.
Sam: Playbook change suggestion: add a prioritization rule `if dedupe_flag = true then urgency = low and route = cs-dedupe-triage` so we avoid owner pings.
Maya: Also want a short-lived `dedupe_ttl` set to now() + interval '21 days' so flags expire if not reviewed. No permanent scoring changes until manual approve.
Priya: Draft backfill update (dry-run): ```
WITH contact_events AS (
  SELECT account_id, user_id, count(*) as events
  FROM telemetry.events
  WHERE event_type = 'login' AND ts >= now() - interval '30 days'
  GROUP BY account_id, user_id
), agg AS (
  SELECT account_id, count(user_id) as unique_users, sum(events) as total_events
  FROM contact_events
  GROUP BY account_id
)
SELECT a.account_id, a.health_score, agg.unique_users, agg.total_events
FROM crm.accounts a
LEFT JOIN agg ON agg.account_id = a.account_id
WHERE a.last_dedupe_ts >= now() - interval '14 days'
LIMIT 100;
```
Priya: If results look sane we'll run an update: ```
UPDATE crm.accounts a
SET dedupe_flag = 'true', dedupe_ttl = now() + interval '21 days', dedupe_review_score_delta = (a.health_score - new_score)::numeric
FROM ( -- compute new_score per account ) s
WHERE a.account_id = s.account_id;
```
Rafael: Ops-bot: can we schedule the dry-run query as a one-off job and post CSV?
Ops-bot: Job scheduled: "cs.dedupe_dryrun_175777" -> will post CSV to /ops/cs/dryruns in ~10m.
Sam: Canary plan: apply dedupe_flag to a random 15% sample of affected accounts (~60 accounts), route to cs-dedupe-triage for 72h, measure variance in renewal triggers and owner escalations.
Maya: Metrics to watch: delta in health_score distribution, number of renewal emails triggered, manual confirmations from CS, any change in churn-risk false positives.
Priya: I'll open a PR with the backfill SQL and sanitizer job. ETA: tomorrow noon PST.
Rafael: QA: I'll validate sample CSV and run quick sanity checks (unique_users > 0, new_score within expected bounds).
Maya: If anything looks off, we rollback flags by running: ```
UPDATE crm.accounts SET dedupe_flag = 'false' WHERE dedupe_ttl < now();
```
Sam: Good rollback. Also add an audit log row for each flagged account so we can trace changes.
CS-bot: Audit event created for 60 accounts in canary group.
Maya: Thanks team. Ping me if you see suspicious mass changes. We'll sync again after the dry-run results are posted. :mag:
Rafael: Will check CSV and post findings in #private-cs-ops.
Priya: Noted. PR link when ready.
Sam: Nice and cautious approach.
